auth.emailNotVerified: Please confirm your email address first. Open the link we emailed you, or send a new one.

empty.to_review: Nothing is waiting for your review.

review.noteHint: Required when you do not accept.

dashboard.recentEmpty: People you open will appear here.

people.addSubtitle: Record what you know — approximate dates and names in any script are welcome.

people.searchPlaceholder: Search by any name, alias or spelling…

toComplete.intro: People added as “unknown for now”. They are not counted as family members, and only you and the tree admins can see them, until they have a name and their relationships are backed by evidence.

toComplete.unverified: Named, but their relationships have no supporting evidence yet.

badge.protectedHint: Living, minor or unknown-status: sensitive details are restricted
badge.provisionalHint: Added as unknown for now; add a name to complete this person
badge.unverifiedHint: Added as unknown for now. Their name is recorded, but their relationships have no supporting evidence yet.

person.editVitalsInTimeline: Edit birth and death details on the Events tab.

err.fixErrors: Please fix the errors above before saving.

form.branchHint: Optional. Adds the person to this branch.
form.livingNotice: For living people and people of unknown status, full birth date, birth time, address and contact are visible to tree admins only by default.
form.namesHint: Add every form of the name you know — birth name, married name, the name in Devanagari or Tamil, aliases. Mark one as preferred.

person.genderIdentityHint: Optional, self-described. Private to the person by default.
person.removeBody: The person will be hidden from the tree. A tree admin can restore them.
person.removeBodyAdmin: The person will be hidden from the tree. You can restore them later from the audit trail.

names.fullAsRecordedHint: Exactly as written in the source, e.g. “Sri Ramaswamy s/o Krishnan”.
names.moreParts: More name parts (patronymic, house name, village prefix, honorifics)
names.scriptHint: Typing in an Indic script selects it automatically.
names.title: Names

err.endBeforeStart: The end year is before the start year.
err.endYearRequired: A range needs an end year.

err.exactNotAllowed: A verbally recalled, approximate or unknown-source time can't be marked exact.

time.timezoneHint: Needed to interpret a birth time correctly (IST for most Indian births).

pickers.placeHint: Type the place exactly as recorded. Pick a suggestion to link it to a known place — the recorded text is always kept.

privacy.claimantCantSeeOverrides: Current overrides are only shown to tree admins. Any level you choose here replaces the existing one.

privacy.fullDateHidden: Full date hidden by privacy settings (year shown)
privacy.label: Privacy

privacy.settingsIntro: Only tree admins and the person themselves (after claiming the profile) can change these settings.
privacy.treeDefaultHint: Uses the tree's default privacy level.

events.preferredHint: When sources disagree (e.g. certificate vs kundli), keep both and mark one preferred.

desc.sibling: Use this when the parents aren't recorded; otherwise siblings are worked out from shared parents.
desc.spouse: Add a marriage or partnership. Multiple and former marriages are supported.

title.spouse: Add a spouse or partner of {{name}}

relatives.unionHint: The other parent is linked automatically.
relatives.unionStart: Date of marriage / start of union

heritage.gotraHint: Suggestions are only a typing aid. Pravara and other facts are never filled in automatically.
heritage.noInference: Heritage details are recorded exactly as the family or a source states them. Vanshavali never infers gotra, pravara, community or anything else from surnames, places or relatives.
heritage.preferredHint: Other values stay as alternatives. Conflicting values are flagged as disputed.
heritage.title: Heritage profile
heritage.valueRequired: Enter a value, or set the status to unknown / withheld.
heritage.templeHint: The temple where the family worships this deity. Pick a place, or type a temple's name to add it as a place of type temple. The deity and the temple are separate facts.

heritage.pravaraNoGotra: Record the gotra from the list first to see pravaras often associated with it. Every pravara stays searchable.

households.noneForPerson: Not a member of any household

relationship.ageQuestionHint: The word for this relative depends on it (e.g. Tau or Chacha). Your answer is saved for the whole family.

treeView.keyboardHelp: Keyboard: Tab to the chart, arrow keys move between people, Enter opens a profile, Space collapses or expands a branch, Home returns to the start. Drag to pan; Ctrl + scroll or the buttons to zoom.
treeView.statusLegend: Side bar on each person: solid = living, broken = deceased, outline = not known. Lifespan and status are also in the List view.

treeView.title: Family tree
treeView.truncated: This view is very large; only the nearest people are shown. Centre on someone further away to see more.

claim.messageHint: e.g. how you're related, or what's recorded here.

claims.subtitleAdmin: Review requests from members who say a profile is theirs
claims.title: Profile claims
claims.viaInvite: Came through an invite link. Check it is really them before approving.
claims.removalExplain: This person asked to be removed from the tree through an invite link. Their profile is already hidden from everyone except tree admins. Erase it, or keep it if the request didn't come from them (for example, a forwarded link).
claims.eraseBody: Their names, dates, notes and other personal details will be deleted and cannot be restored. An anonymous placeholder keeps the family structure intact.

consent.intro: A record of consent given for storing or sharing this person's information (e.g. a parent consenting for a minor).
consent.required: Name, purpose and at least one data category are required.
consent.title: Consent records

members.branchScopeHint: Branch-scoped members can only edit people in that branch.
members.name: Member
members.removeBody: They will lose access to this tree immediately. Family records they added are kept.

members.linkedPerson: Linked to person in the tree

settings.confirmPublicTitle: Publish a public view of this tree?
settings.publicDeceasedHint: A read-only public page lists deceased people marked “Public (deceased only)”.
settings.publicOffHint: Only invited members can see anything in this tree.

public.banner: Public family history — deceased people only
public.deceasedOnly: Only people who have passed away and whose family chose to share them are listed.
public.noPeople: No one is shared publicly yet.

privacyHint.CUSTOM: Tree admins plus people explicitly granted access.
privacyHint.FAMILY_BRANCH: Admins and members of the same family branch.
privacyHint.INVITED_RESEARCHER: All tree members, including invited researchers.
privacyHint.PRIVATE_SELF: Only the person (once they claim the profile) and the tree owner.
privacyHint.PRIVATE_TREE_ADMINS: Only the tree owner and family admins.
privacyHint.PUBLIC_DECEASED_ONLY: Tree members; and the public, if the tree's public view is on and the person has died.
privacyHint.TREE_MEMBERS: Every tree member except invited researchers.

roleHint.BRANCH_ADMIN: Manages people and members of one branch
roleHint.CONTRIBUTOR: Adds and edits people and relationships
roleHint.FAMILY_ADMIN: Full control except deleting the tree
roleHint.REVIEWER: Reviews changes others propose and challenges to facts; edits nothing by itself.

documents.title: Title
documents.subtitle: The family's document vault — certificates, kundlis, deeds and letters
documents.uploadIntro: Files are checked for type and malware, stored encrypted and never altered. Supported certificates and deeds are read by OCR; extracted values wait for your review.
documents.fileHint: PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, audio or video. Up to 50 MB.
documents.privacyHint: Vault categories (certificates, deeds, kundlis) are restricted to admins and custodians regardless.
documents.vaultHint: Stored in the encrypted vault: only admins, document custodians and explicit grants can open the file.
documents.emptyHint: Upload certificates, kundlis, land records, letters and photographs. Only the people allowed to see them will.
documents.noContentAccess: You can see this document's details, but not open the file itself.
documents.ocrNote: Machine-read text. It may contain errors and is not a verified transcription.
documents.deleteTitle: Move document to the recycle bin?
documents.deleteBody: The file is kept and can be restored by a document manager. Links and extracted values stay recorded.
documents.categoryChangeHint: Changing between vault and standard categories may be refused: stored files never move.
documents.versionedHint: Metadata version {{v}}. Every edit keeps the previous version; the original file never changes.
documents.noneForPerson: No documents linked to this person
documents.noneForPersonHint: Upload a birth certificate or kundli to extract details for review.

err.malware_detected: This file was flagged by the malware scanner and was not stored.
err.unsupported_type: This file type isn't supported. Upload a PDF, image, audio or video file.
err.duplicate_document: This exact file has already been uploaded to this tree (same checksum).
err.file_too_large: The file is too large (limit 50 MB).
err.encrypted_pdf: Password-protected PDFs can't be stored. Remove the password and try again.
err.invalid_pdf: The PDF appears to be damaged.
err.invalid_image: The image appears to be damaged.
err.image_too_large: The image dimensions are too large.
err.too_many_pages: The PDF has too many pages.
err.unsafe_pdf: The PDF contains active content (scripts or embedded files) and was refused.
err.scanner_unavailable: The malware scanner is unavailable right now; nothing was stored. Try again later.
err.use_gedcom_import: GEDCOM files are imported from Import / Export, not uploaded as documents.
err.invalid_media: The audio or video file is damaged or contains unsupported content.

extraction.title: Extracted values
extraction.neverOverwrites: Accepting a value records a new claim cited to this document (e.g. a new birth record). Existing facts are never overwritten; disagreements are kept side by side.
extraction.applyToHint: This document isn't linked to a person. Choose who the values are about.
extraction.noneHint: OCR may still be running, the category may not support extraction, or nothing was recognised. You can re-run OCR.
extraction.conflictTitle: Not applied: the record already holds a different value
extraction.conflictBody: Nothing was overwritten. Reject this proposal, or edit it to match — and record the disagreement as a separate claim (e.g. an alternative birth event) if both sources matter.

err.date: Enter a valid date for the chosen precision.
err.time: Enter a valid time; a verbal or unknown-source time can't be exact.
err.pada: Pada is a number from 1 to 4.

astrology.title: Astrology profiles
astrology.noCalculation: Vanshavali records chart details as entered, uploaded or imported. It never calculates a chart or derives one value from another (e.g. rashi from nakshatra).
astrology.calcRequired: Calculated values must record the calculation system and ephemeris version.
astrology.provenance: Where do these values come from?

provHint.entered: Typed in by a family member.
provHint.calculated: Calculated elsewhere — record the software and ephemeris.

astrology.vocabHint: Spellings in any script are recognised.
astrology.privacyHint: Astrology is admin-only by default for living people.
astrology.conflictsIntro: Every recorded birth date, time and place — from certificates, kundlis and family memory — with where it came from. Disagreements are shown, never merged.
astrology.withheld: Some claims are hidden by privacy settings ({{fields}}).

grants.title: Access grants
grants.intro: Custom privacy: tree admins plus the members listed here can see this.
grants.notCustom: Grants apply only when the privacy level is Custom.
grants.none: No one has been granted access.

restore.title: Restore people
restore.subtitle: People removed from the tree can be restored with all their records

merge.title: Compare and merge
merge.description: Merging moves every name, event, relationship, document link and claim to the person you keep. It can be undone from the merge history.
merge.reversible: Every change is recorded so the merge can be undone.

share.hint: Exact fraction, e.g. 1/3 or 1 for the whole.

err.format: Write the share as a fraction like 1/3.
err.decimal: Use a fraction (1/3), not a decimal — shares are kept exact.
err.overWhole: A share can't be more than the whole (1).

partition.title: Record a partition of {{name}}
partition.dateHint: A partition needs a date with at least a year.
partition.scopeHint: The whole property, or one parcel.
partition.endingLegend: Current ownership shares ended by this partition
partition.noneEligible: No current ownership shares in this scope. You can still record a partial deed.
partition.allocIntro: Allocate the {{ended}} being divided among the new holders (people or family branches).
partition.allowPartialHint: Allow allocations that don't add up to the shares ended (e.g. only some co-owners' shares were divided).
partition.warnPartial: Partial deed: {{allocated}} allocated against {{ended}} ended. The difference stays unaccounted for in the record.

err.date: Give the partition date (at least a year).
err.holder: Choose a holder for every allocation.
err.share: Every allocation needs a valid share such as 1/3.
err.overWhole: Allocations add up to more than the whole.
err.nothingEnded: No shares are being ended. Select shares, or mark the deed as partial.
err.unbalanced: Allocations ({{allocated}}) must add up exactly to the shares being divided ({{ended}}), or mark the deed as partial.

partition.noDocuments: No documents linked to this property yet.
partition.summaryBody: {{count}} new holdings totalling {{allocated}} of {{ended}}; {{docs}} documents linked.

property.title: Property register
property.subtitle: Ancestral land and houses — parcels, holders and how they passed down
property.legalNoticeFallback: Genealogical/documentary record only — not a legal title opinion.
property.emptyHint: Record ancestral land, houses and estates with their parcels and the family members who held them.
property.name: Name
property.classificationHint: As the family or documents describe it — not a legal finding.
property.deleteBody: The property record, its parcels, interests and events will be deleted. Documents stay in the vault.
property.overlapping: Recorded ownership claims add up to more than the whole — some claims conflict.
property.statusHint: Documented = supported by a record; asserted = family knowledge.
property.deleteInterestBody: Use this only to correct a mistake. To record that a holding ended, use “End holding”.
property.noInterestsForPerson: No property interests recorded for this person (or none you may see).

parcel.noneHint: Add each plot or survey number separately.
parcel.unitHint: Local units (bigha, guntha…) vary by region and are kept as recorded.
parcel.areaInvalid: Area must be a non-negative number.
parcel.unitRequired: Choose the unit for this area.
parcel.ulpinInvalid: ULPIN must be exactly 14 letters or digits.
parcel.extrasHint: State-specific keys, e.g. “Bhulekh ID” or “RoR no.”.
parcel.extraKeyInvalid: Identifier names may use letters, digits, spaces and _ . - (up to 60).
parcel.recordEvent: Record a subdivision event in the timeline

property.holdersAtHint: Pick a date to see the holders recorded at that time.
property.noHoldersAt: No holdings recorded on that date.
property.noEventsHint: Record acquisitions, inheritance, partitions and mutations to build the history.
property.noDocuments: No documents linked to this property.

gedcom.title: Import / Export
gedcom.subtitle: Move your tree in and out with GEDCOM 7, or download a full family archive
gedcom.exportIntro: A GEDCOM 7 file of what you can see, readable by other genealogy software. Indian details use documented _IND extensions.
gedcom.excludeLivingHint: Recommended when sharing outside the family.
gedcom.includeSensitiveHint: Birth times, astrology, contact and address (admins only). The export is audited.
gedcom.confirmSensitiveBody: The file will contain birth times, astrology, addresses and contact details. Anyone who gets the file can read them. The download is recorded in the audit log.
gedcom.importIntro: Upload a GEDCOM 5.5.1 or 7 file. Nothing is added until you review the report and choose what to do with each person.
gedcom.preservedHint: Kept verbatim so a later export can include them.
gedcom.previewCaption: People to import, possible duplicates and your decision
gedcom.previewLimited: Only the first people are listed; the rest are created by default.
gedcom.photosHint: To bring photos along, put the .ged file and its photos folder (for example “Family Tree_Photos”) in one zip and upload the zip. A GEDZIP (.gdz) file works too.

gedcom.photosNotUploaded_other: This file refers to {{count}} photos, but they weren't uploaded. To import photos, zip the .ged file together with its photos folder and upload the zip instead.
gedcom.photosFound_one: Photos: {{matched}} of {{count}} found in the zip, for {{people}} people. They are checked and added to each person's documents when you import.
gedcom.photosFound_other: Photos: {{matched}} of {{count}} found in the zip, for {{people}} people. They are checked and added to each person's documents when you import.
gedcom.photosSkipped_one: {{count}} photo will be skipped (not in the zip, or more than one file matches)
gedcom.photosSkipped_other: {{count}} photos will be skipped (not in the zip, or more than one file matches)

gedcom.photosImported_other: {{count}} photos imported and linked to people.

gedcom.photosRejected_other: {{count}} files were rejected by the safety checks.

archive.title: Download full family archive
archive.intro: A ZIP with the GEDCOM file, a readable summary and your documents — exactly what you are allowed to see, nothing more.
archive.personalData: The archive contains personal data about your family. Store it securely and share it only with people who should see it.
archive.confirmTitle: Include sensitive data in the archive?
archive.confirmBody: The archive will include sensitive fields and/or vault documents such as certificates and deeds. Anyone with the file can read them. The export is recorded in the audit log.

erase.title: Erase personal data
erase.intro: Permanently erases this person's names, dates, places, notes and other personal data. Use this for a data-erasure request. It can't be undone.
erase.confirmDescription: This cannot be undone or restored.
erase.point1: Names, life events, heritage details, astrology and notes are deleted.
erase.point2: An anonymous placeholder (“Erased person”) stays in the tree so parents, children and spouses remain connected.
erase.point3: The erasure is recorded in the audit log with your reason.
erase.reasonHint: For example, the person's own erasure request.

notice.intro: Vanshavali keeps your family's history. Before you begin, here is what happens to the names and details you add.
notice.private: Your tree is private. Only people you invite can see it, and it is never listed or searchable publicly.
notice.living: Living relatives are protected by default. Birth dates, contact details and addresses stay hidden even from most tree members.
notice.claim: Relatives can claim their own profile, and then they decide who sees their details.
notice.control: You and your relatives can correct, hide or permanently erase a profile at any time.
notice.noSale: We don't sell your data or show ads. Family data is used only to run your tree.

family.intro: Start with yourself and your parents. You can add everyone else later.
family.grandfatherHint: Optional. Added as your father's father, so it needs your father's name.
family.fromLanding: We kept the names you typed on the home page. Check them, then save.

consent.required: Please tick the box to continue.
consent.why: We ask because this tree holds other people's information. Each relative can later claim their profile, change who sees it, or ask for it to be removed.
consent.gateBody: Please confirm this once for this tree. Every member who adds people is asked the same.

invite.intro: Send each living relative a private link so they can claim their own profile and add their side of the family.
invite.safety: Each link works once and expires in 7 days. Opening it doesn't show your tree: you approve each request first.
invite.none: No living relatives to invite yet. You can invite anyone later from their profile.

claimInvite.title: Invite {{name}} to claim their profile
claimInvite.description: Send a private link. After they sign in and confirm it's them, a tree admin approves the request before they can see the tree.
claimInvite.letThemContributeHint: They join as a contributor instead of a viewer. Only tree admins can offer this.
claimInvite.linkFacts: Works once, until {{date}}. Anyone who has the link can ask to claim this profile, so send it only to them. You'll approve before they see anything.
claimInvite.message: Namaste! I've started our family tree on Vanshavali. Open this private link to claim your own profile and add your side of the family: {{url}}

claimLink.title: Claim your family profile
claimLink.signInFirst: A relative invited you to a private family tree. Sign in or create a free account to continue.
claimLink.badLink: This link isn't valid. It may be incomplete or have been cancelled. Ask the relative who sent it for a new one.
claimLink.used: This link has already been used. Ask the relative who sent it for a new one.
claimLink.expired: This link has expired. Ask the relative who sent it for a new one.
claimLink.invitedBy: {{inviter}} added you as “{{person}}” in the private family tree “{{tree}}”.
claimLink.invited: You were added as “{{person}}” in the private family tree “{{tree}}”.
claimLink.noticePrivate: The tree is private and invite-only. Nothing about you is public.
claimLink.noticeReview: A tree admin checks your request before you can see the tree.
claimLink.noticeControl: Once approved, you decide who in the family can see your details.
claimLink.noticeErase: You can withdraw your consent or ask for your profile to be erased at any time.
claimLink.adultHint: A parent or guardian manages profiles of children.
claimLink.adultRequired: You need to be 18 or older to claim a profile yourself.
claimLink.submitted: Thank you. Your request was sent to the tree admins. You'll see the tree here once they approve it.
claimLink.notMeTitle: Not you, or don't want to be in this tree?
claimLink.removeMe: This is me, but remove me
claimLink.notMeConfirmBody: We'll cancel this link so it can't be used again. Nothing about you is saved, and the relative who sent it will see it reached the wrong person.
claimLink.declined: Thanks for letting us know. This link no longer works, and nothing about you was added to the tree.
claimLink.removeBody: Your profile will be hidden straight away from everyone except the tree admins. They will then permanently erase your personal details. Because links can be forwarded, an admin makes the final decision.
claimLink.removeIsMe: I am “{{person}}”, and I want my profile removed
claimLink.removeIsMeRequired: Please confirm that this profile is about you.
claimLink.removeMessageHint: For example, why you'd like to be removed. Please don't include sensitive details.
claimLink.removeConfirm: Hide my profile and ask for removal
claimLink.removalRequested: Done. Your profile is now hidden from everyone except the tree admins, and we've asked them to erase it. You don't need to do anything else.

landing.announce: A living archive of Indian family heritage

hero.eyebrow: Tradition and reverence, kept for every generation
hero.lead: Vanshavali is a home for your family's story — the names your elders remember, the village your great-grandparents left, the gotra and kuladevi your family honours, and the papers that show where the land came from. Kept safely, in your own languages, for the generations still to come.
hero.sceneAlt: Image: a Tambool offering laid out on a jute cloth in a traditional courtyard. Two betel leaves, whole supari, marigold petals and rudraksha beads surround a wooden plaque reading “परंपरा एवं श्रद्धा — Voices of Heritage, Connecting generations”, with clay pots, a charpai and string lights behind.
hero.sceneCaption: Tambool — betel leaf, supari and flowers, offered with reverence at every family occasion.

purpose.p1a: For centuries, the pandas of Haridwar, Gaya and Pushkar wrote our families into hand-kept bahis, and our grandmothers carried the rest in memory: which village we came from, which temple we visit, who married into which family. These are not just names — they are
purpose.p1b: each one tying a living family to everyone who came before.
purpose.p2: brings that same care to a new medium: a private archive where a family records its people, its relationships, its rites and its records — together, in Hindi and English.

educate.title: To Educate
educate.body: Help every child know who their great-grandparents were, where the family comes from, and what each relationship is called.

preserve.title: To Preserve
preserve.body: Keep names, dates, places and papers safe before the people who remember them are gone.

celebrate.title: To Celebrate
celebrate.body: Honour the rites, the festivals and the elders that hold a joint family together across cities and continents.

archive.lead: Begin with yourself, or with the eldest ancestor anyone remembers. Add parents, spouses and children, and watch the generations grow into a tree your whole family can explore.

card.title: Family Tree Builder
card.body: Build your tree generation by generation, with names in every script your family has used, dates as exact or as approximate as memory allows, and every kind of bond — by birth, adoption, ritual or marriage.

kinship.title: Relationships in your words.
kinship.body: Ask how two people are related and hear दादा, नानी, मामा or बुआ — not just “uncle”.

heritage.title: Heritage beside each name.
heritage.body: Gotra, kuladevi, mool gaon and family traditions, kept with the person they belong to.

together.title: Built together.
together.body: Invite relatives to add their own branches; you decide who can view and who can edit.

private.title: Private by default.
private.body: Living relatives are visible only to the family members you invite.

archive.alt: An animated family tree growing generation by generation: Suresh and Kamala Sharma, their sons Ramesh and Mahesh with their wives Sunita and Geeta, and grandchildren Aarav, Anaya and Kabir. It ends by naming the relationship: Suresh is Aarav's dādā, his father's father.
archive.caption: Built the way families build theirs: one generation at a time. Those who have passed away show their years; the lock marks living relatives whose details stay within the family.
archive.note: Sign in or create an account to start. Your tree stays private unless you choose otherwise.

tree.title: The Sharma family tree
tree.kin: Suresh is Aarav's दादा (dādā) — his father's father

leaf.subtitle: The sacred leaf
leaf.p1: Before almost every auspicious beginning — a wedding, a griha pravesh, a puja — there is the betel leaf: heart-shaped, deep green, laid on the thali before anything else is placed upon it.
leaf.p2: Offered to deities and to guests alike as tambula, the paan leaf says the same thing in every region: you are welcome here. In Vanshavali, those beginnings are kept too — every sanskar and ceremony can be recorded on the people it belonged to, with the date and the place.
leaf.quote: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति
leaf.quoteMeaning: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water…
leaf.imgAlt: A heart-shaped betel leaf resting on jute, beside whole supari and rudraksha beads.

offered.label: Offered as
offered.body: Tambula — leaf, supari and lime, given to guests and deities.

petal.subtitle: The fragrant offering
petal.p1: Flowers are the language of devotion. Marigolds, bright as the saffron of a sadhu's robe, are strung into garlands for doorways and wedding mandaps and scattered before every deity.
petal.p2: The same garlands mark a family's turning points: the bride and groom exchanging jaimala, a portrait garlanded in memory of an elder. In Vanshavali, marriages and unions are recorded with their dates, and the children of each union stay with it.
petal.quoteMeaning: Treat your mother as divine. Treat your father as divine.
petal.imgAlt: Orange marigold petals scattered on jute around a whole supari nut.
petal.imgCaption: Genda · the flower of every festival

marigold.label: Marigold
marigold.body: Garlands for doorways, mandaps and deities.

jasmine.label: Jasmine
jasmine.body: Woven into hair and offered at dusk.

lotus.label: Lotus
lotus.body: The seat of Lakshmi and Saraswati.

seed.subtitle: The auspicious completion
seed.p1: A whole supari, unbroken, is placed with care on the puja thali. In many homes it stands for Lord Ganesha himself, so that every ritual begins — and is completed — in his presence.
seed.p2: Wholeness is what a family archive is for: no branch forgotten, no elder left out. Vanshavali keeps the whole family together — joint families and households, every branch, and the heritage they share: gotra and pravara, kuladevata and kuladevi, the mool gaon.
seed.quote: सं गच्छध्वं सं वदध्वं सं वो मनांसि जानताम्
seed.quoteMeaning: Walk together, speak together, let your minds be of one accord.
seed.imgAlt: Two whole supari nuts on jute, with rudraksha beads and a betel leaf behind.

whole.label: Kept whole
whole.body: Often stands for Lord Ganesha in the puja.

shared.label: Given with paan
shared.body: Completes the tambula offered to guests.

keepers.lead: Every family has them. Their memories are the archive; Vanshavali only gives them a place to stay.

elder.title: The grandmother
elder.body: She knows which great-aunt married into which village, what the kuladevi is called, and the year of the flood. Sit with her, and record it while you can.

panda.title: The pilgrim's bahi
panda.role: kept by the pandas for centuries
panda.body: At Haridwar, Gaya and Pushkar, families still find their forefathers' names in registers written by hand, generation after generation. Their entries become sources in your tree.

grandchild.title: The grandchild
grandchild.body: Living in another city, or another country, but asking the questions that keep the thread unbroken: who were they, and where did we come from?

samskara.title: The Sixteen Samskaras: Rites of Passage in a Hindu Life
samskara.body: From namakarana to vivaha to antyeshti, the samskaras mark each stage of a life — and each one is a date and a place a family wants to remember.
samskara.inApp: In Vanshavali: record each ceremony as an event on the person

gotra.title: Gotra, Pravara & the Science of Lineage
gotra.body: A gotra traces a family to a rishi; the pravara names the rishis of that line. Many families still recall them at every wedding.
gotra.inApp: In Vanshavali: keep gotra and pravara with each person — never guessed from a surname

kuladevata.title: Kuladevata: The Family Deity That Travels With You
kuladevata.body: Families move across states and continents, but the kuladevata and kuladevi stay — honoured at every mundan, wedding and homecoming.
kuladevata.inApp: In Vanshavali: record kuladevata, kuladevi and the family temple

nakshatra.title: The Nakshatras: Reading the Stars Like Our Grandmothers Did
nakshatra.body: A birth time remembered as “just before sunrise, on Diwali” is still worth keeping — it is how a kundali was once cast.
nakshatra.inApp: In Vanshavali: save a birth time with how exact it is and where it came from

vedic.title: The Vedic gotras
vedic.body: Families begin to trace their descent to the rishis — the gotra lineages still named at weddings today.

shraddha.title: Shraddha and Pitru Paksha
shraddha.body: Remembering the ancestors by name becomes a yearly duty, carried from parent to child.

puranic.title: The Puranic vamshas
puranic.body: The Puranas set down long genealogies — the solar and lunar dynasties — as sacred history.

bahi.title: The pandas' bahis
bahi.body: At pilgrimage towns, family priests record every visiting family in hand-written registers, generation after generation.

partition.title: A nation scattered
partition.body: Partition and migration separate millions of families from their villages, their records and each other.

today.title: The digital vanshavali
today.body: Families gather what remains — memories, papers and photographs — into one private archive they own together.

join.lead: Start with one name. Ask one elder one question. The rest of the tree will follow.
join.note: Living relatives stay private. Export your tree as a standard GEDCOM file whenever you wish.

footer.tagline: Preserving the threads of tradition, connecting generations.
footer.dataCredit: Place names: Local Government Directory, Government of India, and India Post, under the Government Open Data Licence – India.

plant.lead: Type four names and watch three generations take root. When you're ready, keep it as a private tree of your own.

status.empty: Start with your own name — the first leaf of the tree.
status.started: It's taking root. Add another name to grow the next branch.
status.complete: Three generations of {{surname}} — your vanshavali has begun.

plant.note: These names stay in this browser tab until you create your account. Nothing is uploaded yet, and your tree is private by default.

how.lead: Begin with one name tonight. The tree grows as the family remembers.

seed.title: Plant the seed
seed.body: Start a private tree with yourself — or with the eldest ancestor anyone still remembers. You can try it on this page before you sign up.

memories.title: Gather the elders' memories
memories.body: Sit with your grandparents and add parents, spouses and children from any profile. Dates can be exact or approximate — “about 1925” — and photos and documents can sit alongside.

invite.title: Invite the family
invite.body: Invite relatives by email with the role you choose, or send a private WhatsApp link so someone can claim their own profile.

trust.lead: A family tree holds living people as well as ancestors. These protections are built into how Vanshavali works, not just written in a policy.

private.title: Private and invite-only
private.body: A new tree can be opened only by the relatives you invite. Nobody else can see who is in it.

living.title: Living relatives protected
living.body: For anyone living, birth dates and times, phone numbers and addresses are shown only to tree admins — and to that relative once their claim to the profile is approved.

control.title: You decide who sees what
control.body: Every member has a role, from viewer to family admin, and every person has their own privacy level. Public pages stay off unless the owner turns them on, and even then show only relatives who have passed away and are marked public one by one.

yours.title: Your records stay yours
yours.body: Owners, family admins and contributors can download the tree as a standard GEDCOM file, or the whole family archive, at any time.

geo.fieldsetHint: Add what you know. Coordinates are optional; an approximate location is better than none.
geo.precisionHint: Never claim more precision than you have.
geo.sourceHint: e.g. family memory, survey map, GPS on a visit
geo.noteHint: Provenance, landmarks, how to find it.
geo.coordinatePrivacyHint: Others see it rounded to about 11 km. Public pages never show coordinates.
geo.coarsenedEdit: You see this place's coordinates rounded for privacy, so you can't change them here.
geo.latError: Enter a latitude between -90 and 90 and a longitude between -180 and 180.
geo.pairError: Enter both latitude and longitude, or neither.
geo.noPoints: Nothing to show on the map yet. Add coordinates to places or events.
geo.noTiles: Simplified map without third-party tiles; boundaries are not drawn.
geo.tableCaption: Locations shown on the map of {{title}}

lifeEvents.heading: Life events
lifeEvents.categoryHint: Sets the event type for you.
lifeEvents.title: Title
lifeEvents.visibilityHint: Photos added to it are never more visible than this.
lifeEvents.coordinatesHint: Use when the place itself has no coordinates or the event happened at a specific spot.
lifeEvents.pageSubtitle: Ceremonies, milestones and memories across the family — with photos, places and reminders.
lifeEvents.noneHint: Add naming ceremonies, weddings, migrations, awards and other milestones from a person's Events tab.
lifeEvents.whoHint: Choose the person the event is mainly about.

photos.albumHint: Photos are stored privately in the document vault and shown only to people allowed to see them.

photos.caption: Caption
photos.privacyInherited: The photo gets the stricter of the event's and the person's privacy.

reminders.dialogHint: Only you get this reminder for "{{event}}". You can stop it at any time.
reminders.customDaysHint: e.g. 3, 30 — up to six reminders in total
reminders.customDaysError: Use whole days from 0 to 365, separated by commas.
reminders.everyYearHint: Birthdays, anniversaries and remembrance days repeat every year.
reminders.onceHint: Turn on to be reminded of this date every year.
reminders.channelsHint: SMS and WhatsApp messages never include names; they link back here.
reminders.testSent: A test reminder is on its way.
reminders.pageSubtitle: Birthdays, anniversaries and remembrance days you choose to be reminded of. Only you see your reminders.
reminders.noneUpcomingHint: Dates appear here when birthdays, weddings or deaths have a full date you can see.
reminders.noneMineHint: Use "Remind me" on an upcoming date or on any life event.
reminders.enabled: Send me reminders for this tree
reminders.enabledHint: Turning this off pauses all your reminders here.
reminders.phones: Phone numbers for SMS and WhatsApp
reminders.phonesHint: Your number is encrypted, never shown in full, and used only after you confirm it with a code.
reminders.phonesUnavailable: SMS and WhatsApp reminders are not available on this server yet. Email reminders work.
reminders.codeSent: We sent a code to that number.

cancelReason.no_longer_visible: The event is no longer visible to you
cancelReason.not_a_member: You are no longer a member
cancelReason.date_hidden: The full date is hidden from you

render.title: Animated video
render.hint: Rendered on the server from what you can see; private people stay private. Start with a quick preview image.
render.unavailable: Animated exports are not enabled on this server.

timelinePage.title: Family timeline
timelinePage.subtitle: Who lived when, how lives overlapped, and the family's important events across the years.

viz.title: Charts & maps
viz.subtitle: See the family as a fan, a web of relatives, a pedigree, a tree, lives across time, a life story or a map.

chartHint.fan: Ancestors in a fan: spot birthplace and village patterns and research gaps.
chartHint.graph: Explore the extended family: expand branches, drag people, find connections.
chartHint.pedigree: A classic pedigree chart, clean for printing.
chartHint.family: Ancestors or descendants as a family tree.
chartHint.lifespan: Who lived when, and how generations overlapped.
chartHint.events: A person's life events in order, with photos.
chartHint.map: Ancestral villages, homes, temples, events and migrations.

viz.graphSummary: {{count}} people and {{edges}} relationships loaded. Expand people marked + to load more.

viz.withoutDates_one: {{count}} person without a known birth year is not shown.
viz.withoutDates_other: {{count}} people without a known birth year are not shown.

home.clickHint: Click anyone to open their story
home.emptyTitle: Your vanshavali starts with one name
home.emptyBody: Add yourself, a parent or the eldest ancestor you know. The family will grow here, generation by generation, as you add relatives.
home.onlyOne: No children are recorded for {{name}} yet
home.addRelatives: Add their children, spouse or parents

smartAdd.title: Add a relative of {{name}}
smartAdd.desc: Choose the relationship. We'll use relatives already in the tree and show you everything before saving.
smartAdd.whom: Whom do you want to add?

ageNote.elder: Choosing someone here records that they are older than {{name}}.
ageNote.younger: Choosing someone here records that they are younger than {{name}}.

smartAdd.hiddenNote_one: One recorded relative here is private to you. Ask a tree admin if they are the right person.
smartAdd.hiddenNote_other: {{count}} recorded relatives here are private to you. Ask a tree admin if one of them is the right person.
smartAdd.noOptions: There is no one to choose here, and a new person can't be added at this step. Use the family panel instead, or ask a tree admin.

blocked.two_biological_parents: This person already has two biological parents recorded, so another one can't be added here.

smartAdd.birthYearHint: Optional — an approximate year is fine
smartAdd.sexHint: Optional. Choosing a relationship does not record sex at birth; enter it only if you know it.
smartAdd.moreLater: You can add dates, places, photos and other names later from their profile.

preview.explicitSibling: Linked directly as a brother or sister (their parents aren't recorded yet).

smartSelect.addOwn: Add “{{text}}” as your family's own entry

offers.dialogIntro: Reviewers may merge it with similar entries. Only the name, its other spellings and what you write below are shared; your family is never named.
offers.noteHint: Do not include names of family members.

traditions.title: Family traditions
traditions.subtitle: Ritual guides, customs, songs, recipes and stories your family keeps.
traditions.emptyHint: Write down how your family does things: a puja, a wedding custom, a song, Dadi's recipe.
traditions.withdrawBody: It will no longer be shown. Its history is kept.
traditions.tooLong: The text is too long (at most 50,000 characters).
traditions.bodyHint: Plain text. Leave a blank line between paragraphs, start a line with - for a list, and wrap words in ** for bold.
traditions.peopleHint: Mentioning someone never changes who can read this entry.
traditions.rationaleRequired: Say why this change is right.
traditions.reviewNotice: Your family reviews changes to entries other people wrote. This change is sent for review.
traditions.sent: Sent for review. The change appears once a reviewer approves it.
